questions: Does the incorporated Circular or Ordinance impose additional conditions beyond the selected three-factor antecedent? Those materials are not supplied, and their effect is outside this predicate.

assumptions: This predicate concerns the selected applicability condition, not whole-law compliance or licence possession.
Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.
The declared input vocabulary is supplied for this controlled comparison; its adequacy as a legal abstraction remains unverified.
The three facts refer to the same family office, services and business; applicable regulated-activity carve-outs have already been resolved.
“All of which” refers to the complete three-factor list, and “must be present” requires their conjunction.
True means that the selected three-factor antecedent is satisfied; it does not establish that those factors exhaust every legal requirement.

citations.quote: all of which must be present

firstly, the services provided by the family office constitute one or more regulated activity as defined under the Ordinance; secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.
What amounts to “carrying on a business in Hong Kong” is not defined in the Ordinance and will need to be determined by reference to the facts of each case

readings.distinction: The possible necessity-only and jointly-sufficient readings of “in order to give rise to a licensing obligation” differ about the ultimate obligation, but yield the same conjunction for the requested antecedent. No rival connective parse is defensible: “all” attaches to all three enumerated factors, the final “and” confirms conjunction, and the target contains no negation. “One or more” concerns regulated activities within the first factor, not alternatives among the three factors. Accordingly, only one antecedent reading is retained.

vocabulary_concerns: The vocabulary captures the three-factor conjunction but does not determine the case-dependent legal classifications underlying its inputs. In particular, the contextual qualifications concerning business activity remain external to business and hong_kong.

The vocabulary cannot distinguish necessary conditions for an ultimate licensing obligation from an exhaustive sufficient legal test. That distinction does not change the selected antecedent and must not be resolved by treating its Boolean result as a complete licensing verdict.
